description:
Every fact that the packaged profile and the adopter configuration reference restate is derived from its authority rather than kept in agreement by hand.

## Background

Three facts in this repository exist as two copies each, held correct by an assertion or by nothing at all.

The packaged profile embeds its whole directory into the binary at compile time, so an asset an adopter receives must live inside that directory. This repository also consumes the same files live at their working paths. The result is 62 asset pairs, each carried twice in the tree. A test asserts every pair byte-identical, executable mode included, so drift fails the suite rather than shipping. Both copies are still hand-maintained, and keeping them equal is a step a contributor must remember on every edit.

The planning-bracket template declaration has no such guard. It is embedded inline in the profile manifest rather than shipped as an asset, so the byte-equality contract that covers the 62 pairs does not reach it. The two declarations agree today because one change happened to touch both.

The adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration restate the managed, permanent, and issue-scoped area lists in prose. Their authority is the shipped documentation-policy constant, and an existing renderer already turns that constant into TOML. The reference cites the constant by name, which orients a reader, but nothing binds the values. These lists went stale during earlier work and blocked two reviews before they were repaired.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration obtain the managed, permanent, and issue-scoped area lists from the shipped documentation-policy constant, and neither document retains a hand-maintained second copy of any of those lists.
- [hard] REQ-02: A change to either the repository planning-bracket template declaration or its packaged counterpart, without the corresponding change to the other, fails the test suite. The guard compares the two parsed declarations rather than a hand-written expectation of their contents.
- [hard] REQ-03: The packaged live-asset tree is derived from the repository files it mirrors rather than carried as a second checked-in copy, and editing a live file alone cannot leave the packaged copy stale.
- [hard] REQ-04: A build from unchanged sources and unchanged explicit environment stays byte-for-byte reproducible, and the derivation is ordered so that the embedded package always reads a fully populated tree.

## Notes

REQ-03 changes a declared binary build input, so every downstream verdict rebuilds once it lands.

The ordering in REQ-04 is the load-bearing risk. The embedding macro reads the package directory at compile time; a derivation that runs after it produces a silently stale binary rather than an error, which is the one failure mode this change must not introduce.

Upholds `@/invariant/single-source-prose`.
title: Derived profile assets and projected policy documentation
